title: Runbook-as-Typed-API Saga Orchestrator
creator: Jordan Lin
description:
Problem: Existing runbook/playbook work at Redwood is a mix of scripts, ad-hoc task lists, and data-driven templates. Operators repeatedly rebuild step glue to expose runbooks to external services (Slack, PagerDuty, internal CLIs). We need a safer, typed surface that turns runbooks into first-class, triggerable APIs with saga semantics: explicit step inputs/outputs, compensating actions, idempotency guarantees, and observable execution traces.

Goal: Build a Runbook-as-Typed-API system and a lightweight Saga Orchestrator that lets engineers and SREs: 1) define runbooks as a sequence of typed steps (OpenAPI-style schemas for step inputs/outputs), 2) expose them as stable HTTP/CLI endpoints with auto-generated client stubs, 3) support dry-run and validation modes, 4) provide compensating/rollback actions for long-running multi-step repair flows, 5) produce audit-friendly execution records and per-step metrics for Console and incident timelines.

Scope: MVP focuses on internal admin utilities (no public externalization). Components: typed runbook manifest (YAML/JSON schema), orchestrator service implementing saga pattern with persistent state and checkpointing, runtime step adaptor library (JS/Go) for executing step primitives, dry-run validator, UI hooks for the Console timeline, and a small gating layer for RBAC+approval on high-privilege runbooks.

Trade-offs considered: 1) heavyweight workflow engines (Cadence/Temporal) provide rich guarantees but add operational burden; we will implement a minimal persistent saga store with deterministic replay and checkpointing to keep runtime simple. 2) Strict typing improves safety but increases authoring cost; adopt optional quick-mode for exploratory runbooks with an explicit opt-in toggle. 3) Compensating actions are required for safety but cannot cover every external side-effect; require runbook authors to mark irreversible steps and add human approval gates for those.

Success criteria: reduced mean-time-to-remediate for common incidents, fewer one-off scripts in ops Slack, and improved traceability for compliance audits.
acceptance_criteria: Define at least three example runbooks in typed manifest format (network-evict-cache, rotate-gpu, scale-dedicated-pool)
Expose runbooks as stable HTTP endpoints with OpenAPI schema and generated TypeScript/Go client stubs
Orchestrator persists per-run state in the saga store; runs can be resumed after controller restart
Support dry-run mode that validates types, simulates steps, and emits an execution preview without performing side-effects
Implement compensating action hooks and a human-approval gate for irreversible steps
Emit per-step telemetry (start, success, failure, duration) and a run-level audit record visible in Console timeline
engineering_notes: 2026-02-12: Spike complete. Prototype orchestration using Postgres for saga state and a lightweight worker pool. Trade-off: avoids new infra but needs migration plan for scale.
2026-02-18: Decided on manifest schema v1: top-level runbook metadata, typed step list, step timeouts, compensating_step reference, human_approval boolean. Draft in repo at /ops/runbook-manifests/v1
2026-02-26: Implemented step adaptor SDK in TypeScript (repo PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-orch/pull/1257). Adaptor provides standardized start/complete/fail hooks and retry helpers.
2026-03-03: Added dry-run validator that performs JSON-schema validation and a mock executor for preview. Found mismatch patterns for legacy scripts; added migration lint rules.

2026-03-07: Security review kickoff with Security. Primary requirement: all privileged runbooks must require RBAC group + explicit approval. See audit notes in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-orch/pull/1289
2026-03-10: Performance note — frequent short runs cause DB churn. Plan: introduce KV cache for ephemeral runs and a batch checkpoint flusher in next cycle.

2026-03-12: Integration tests added to CI. End-to-end test covers happy path, dry-run, compensating action, and resume-after-failure. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-orch/pull/1312 landed in staging branch.
Open questions: how to handle secrets in runbook inputs (KMS envelope vs. secret refs), and retention policy for run audit records (90d vs. 1y).
qa_plan: Unit tests for manifest parser and step adaptor SDK
E2E tests in staging: simulate a failing step, verify compensating action executes and run resumes after orchestrator restart
Dry-run acceptance tests that assert no side-effects and correct preview payloads
Fuzz invalid manifests to ensure validator rejects bad shapes with clear errors
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (internal alpha): enable for a small set of SREs and Platform engineers (opt-in namespace) - 2 weeks
Stage 2 (beta): widen to all internal operators, integrate Console timeline hooks and per-run telemetry - 3 weeks
Stage 3 (GA): add RBAC gating, retention policy, and internal docs. Migrate critical runbooks from ad-hoc scripts to typed manifests
Fallback: revert flag to disable new orchestrator and route requests to legacy scripts via compatibility adapter
comments: PM (Elias): +1 on typed guarantees — ask to include sample client stubs for platform teams
